item.title: Russia's jet-powered drones bring empty Kyiv supermarket shelves and rattle Ukrainians
item.description: Russian forces relentlessly battered Kyiv and cities in the region around the Ukrainian capital for a fifth straight day, leaving some supermarket shelves bare after repeated strikes on warehouses.

item.title: Singapore is scrambling to stabilize birthrates. Experts say there are lessons for the U.S.
item.description: Singapore has unveiled a national initiative built entirely around its collapsing birthrate. Some demographers say the plan includes policy ideas that could help American parents.

item.title: The U.S. Venezuela oil deal won't lower your gas prices. Here's what you need to know
item.description: The Trump administration announced a deal Friday to develop a vast amount of Venezuela's oil reserves, with the U.S. taking a majority stake. Energy experts say there are many reasons to be skeptical.

item.title: Why too many women are prescribed antibiotics for UTIs they don't have
item.description: A recent study found that many women treated for recurrent UTIs didn't have UTIs at all. Instead, their symptoms were caused by hormonally driven inflammation and pelvic floor dysfunction.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: NPR spent 2 years tracking deaths from heat. We found a staggering hidden toll
item.description: An NPR investigation found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat much more often than official counts show. We explore the reasons why — and how lives can be saved.

item.title: Arizona's taps won't run dry, but water bills will go up under federal plan for Colorado River
item.description: New federal rules mean Arizona will be getting a lot less water from the Colorado river. City leaders say they've been planning for years and no one will run out, but keeping taps flowing is expensive.
